description: v3 stress corpus — deliberately harder than heavy_stutter_test_scripts.json (v2). Built 2026-07-25 to answer 'make it messier and see what breaks'.
design_notes: v2 modelled only what Whisper actually emits: dropped content plus canonical hallucination phrases. v3 keeps those and adds two harder families.

FAMILY A (verbatim): raw human-transcription style, e.g. 's-s-s-stuttering', as found in FluencyBank and UCLASS. Whisper never emits this, so the engine is being fed a distribution it does not normally see. This is a hard test of DisfluencyFilter, not a simulation of a typical day.
FAMILY B (stacked): several disfluency types inside one utterance — block plus repetition plus prolongation plus filler plus a hallucination — so no single rule can carry the case.

FAMILY C (destroyed): the intended content is genuinely NOT recoverable from the input. Correct behaviour is to preserve what survived and NOT invent the missing part. These cases are scored to catch confident fabrication, which is the failure mode that actually matters in a product that pastes into other people's documents. A high score on these would be bad news, not good.

cases.type: verbatim part-word repetitions, FluencyBank style
cases.intended: I would say stuttering shaped how I talk to people
cases.disfluent: i'd say s-s-s uhm s-s-s-stuttering shaped how i t-t-talk to p-p-people
cases.notes: Lifted in style directly from published FluencyBank transcript lines. Three separate part-word repetition sites plus an interjection. Whisper would never produce this shape.

cases.type: word repetition plus part-word repetition in one clause
cases.intended: With stuttering early on I definitely avoided the phone
cases.disfluent: with with s-s-stuttering early on d-d-d-definitely i i i avoided the ph- ph- phone
cases.notes: Word-level and sound-level repetition interleaved. The natural-repeats guard must not fire on 'i i i'.

cases.type: prolongations written as letter runs
cases.intended: So I called the office and asked for Monday instead
cases.disfluent: sooooo i c-c-called the offfffice and aaaasked for m-m-monday instead
cases.notes: Stretched sounds written as repeated characters. Engine must normalise without eating real doubled letters ('office').

cases.type: broken word, abandonment mid-syllable, restart
cases.intended: I need to reschedule the appointment with Doctor Weaver
cases.disfluent: i need to resche- resche- i need to reschedule the appoint- the appointment with d-d-doctor w-w-weaver
cases.notes: Broken word plus full-phrase restart plus blocked proper noun. Proper noun must survive.

cases.type: four disfluency types stacked in one utterance
cases.intended: Can you send me the contract before Friday afternoon
cases.disfluent: can can you uhm ssssend me the thanks for watching contract before f-f-f um friday afternoon
cases.notes: Word repetition, filler, prolongation, hallucination insertion, and a part-word repetition on the target day. Everything at once.

cases.type: two separate Whisper hallucinations in one utterance
cases.intended: I wanted to talk about the budget for the second quarter
cases.disfluent: i wanted to thank you for watching talk about the budget for the subscribe second quarter
cases.notes: Two canonical Whisper-on-silence artifacts at two different block sites. Both must be removed without taking real content with them.

cases.type: block destroys the negation — meaning-flip risk
cases.intended: I do not want to cancel the order
cases.disfluent: i do thanks for watching want to c-c-cancel the order
cases.notes: The hallucination sits exactly where 'not' was. Naive cleanup yields the OPPOSITE instruction. This is the single most dangerous shape in the corpus — the SAFE-mode meaning guard exists for this. Reconstructing it as an affirmative is a serious failure, not a small one.

cases.type: blocks around a number and a date
cases.intended: Transfer four thousand two hundred dollars on March fifteenth
cases.disfluent: transfer f-f-four thousand t-t-t two hundred d-d-dollars on m-m-march thanks for watching fifteenth
cases.notes: Numbers and a date under repeated blocks plus a hallucination adjacent to the day. Digits and dates must survive exactly.

cases.type: long utterance, five disfluency sites across three clauses
cases.intended: I spoke to the landlord yesterday and he said the repairs will start next week but I still need the notice in writing
cases.disfluent: i i spoke to the l-l-landlord yesterday and and he said the repairs will thanks for watching start next week but i i still need the n-n-notice in in writing
cases.notes: Length plus repetition density. Tests whether reconstruction degrades over a long span or holds.

cases.type: covert avoidance — talks around the word, then lands it
cases.intended: I need to call the pharmacy about my prescription
cases.disfluent: i need to uhm reach out to the the place where you get medicine the ph- the pharmacy about my p-p-prescription
cases.notes: The speaker routes around 'pharmacy', describes it, then reaches it. Good output collapses the detour without losing the real target word.

cases.type: Russian filler and repetition inside an English sentence
cases.intended: I will send the documents to my brother tomorrow morning
cases.disfluent: i will ну ну s-s-send the d-d-documents to my брат uh brother tomorrow эээ morning
cases.notes: Russian fillers 'ну ну' and 'эээ' plus a Russian word the speaker immediately self-translates. Fillers go, the English target stays, no Russian leaks into the output.

cases.type: Whisper repetition loop artifact
cases.intended: The meeting is in the conference room
cases.disfluent: the meeting is in the conference room conference room conference room conference room conference room
cases.notes: Whisper's decoder-loop failure, not the speaker. Distinct from a stutter: identical multi-word span repeated many times at the tail. Must collapse to one.

cases.type: full sentence abandoned, different sentence completed
cases.intended: Actually let me just email you the address
cases.disfluent: the the the house is on uh it's near the i mean actually let me just e-e-email you the address
cases.notes: Speaker abandons a whole line of thought and restarts with different content. Only the completed thought should survive.

cases.type: block on a personal name, plus filler stack
cases.intended: Hi this is George calling about the appointment
cases.disfluent: hi this is uhm uh g- g- g- thanks for watching george calling about the a-a-appointment
cases.notes: Blocking on your own name is the canonical high-stakes case. The name must come out clean and correct.

cases.type: question broken by blocks, punctuation absent
cases.intended: Could you tell me whether the package arrived today
cases.disfluent: c-c-could you t-t-tell me whether the p-p-package uhm subscribe arrived today
cases.notes: Every content word blocked, one hallucination, no punctuation from ASR. Must stay a question.

cases.type: maximum density — every type present
cases.intended: I am going to the store to buy bread and milk
cases.disfluent: i i i am g-g-going to the the the ssssstore store store to to b-b-buy uhm thanks for watching bread and m-m-milk
cases.notes: The shape the operator described verbatim: tripled words, blocked onsets, prolongation, filler, hallucination, all in one short sentence.

cases.type: the key noun never made it out of the mouth
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — the object of the sentence was lost in the block
cases.disfluent: i need to pick up the thanks for watching from the store before six
cases.notes: The thing being picked up is simply absent. Correct behaviour: keep the recoverable frame, do NOT invent a plausible noun. Any confident specific object here is fabrication.

cases.type: proper noun destroyed
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — the name was lost
cases.disfluent: please forward the file to subscribe at the london office
cases.notes: A person's name was blocked away. Inventing a name here would be the worst possible output — it is confidently wrong and would be pasted into a real email.

cases.type: amount destroyed
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — the figure was lost
cases.disfluent: the invoice came to thanks for watching dollars which is more than we agreed
cases.notes: Money figure gone. Fabricating a number is unacceptable. Correct output preserves the complaint without a figure.

cases.type: second half of the utterance never emerged
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — the conditional's consequence was lost
cases.disfluent: if the tenant does not pay by the first then i i i uhm thanks for watching
cases.notes: The consequence clause is entirely missing. Completing it would be the model writing the user's legal position for them.

cases.type: surviving text supports two opposite readings
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — cannot tell which meaning was intended
cases.disfluent: tell them we c-c-can subscribe make the deadline
cases.notes: Whatever was blocked could have been 'can' or 'cannot', or an adverb flipping the sense. Picking one silently is a coin flip presented as certainty.

cases.type: nothing but artifacts survived
cases.intended: UNRECOVERABLE — no real content present
cases.disfluent: thanks for watching uhm thanks for watching subscribe
cases.notes: A long block where Whisper emitted only its own artifacts. Correct output is empty or near-empty. Producing a fluent sentence from this is pure invention.
